summary: Frontend-only regression test for the tab-switch delay fix in /app/frontend/src/app/template.tsx (0.35s opacity+Y slide -> 0.18s opacity-only fade). All 7 top-nav tabs navigate to correct routes with responsive timings and no slide+fade lag. Contact form submits successfully. Logo swap and header scroll-state transition work. No JS errors introduced.
critical_code_review_comments: template.tsx transition is correct (0.18s opacity-only easeOut).
Next.js dev-mode webpack-hmr WSS 502 warning is expected in preview and not user-facing.
Console warning about scroll-behavior:smooth on <html>: consider adding data-scroll-behavior="smooth" for future Next.js compat (minor).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tab-switch timings measured (click -> URL match -> main opacity>0.9): about 432ms, cyber-services 408ms, solutions 366ms, industries 377ms, tech-partners 1762ms (cold first-load in dev), blog 711ms, contact 660ms. Revisits: 263-323ms. These are dev-mode fetch times (per agent-to-agent note); the previously-visible 0.35s slide+fade lag is gone. Contact form POST /api/contact returned 200 and contact-success testid was rendered. Logo swap: on homepage top the header is transparent over dark hero and after scrolling header bg becomes rgba(255,255,255,0.9) with the blue+red colored mits logo visible. No page JS errors captured across full nav flow.
rca of the issue: Original lag was caused by every route-change animating opacity 0->1 AND translateY 14px->0 over 0.35s in template.tsx, giving a visible slide+fade before content appeared. Fix reduced this to a 0.18s opacity-only easeOut, eliminating the perceived transition lag while keeping a subtle fade. Verified: no stuck opacity-0 states, no regressions in scroll reveals, header logo swap, or contact submission.
